title: log-record.v1: one structured log line (0.13.0)
description: Every Parity service writes its logs as NDJSON on stdout or stderr: one object per line, at most 16000 bytes (UTF-8, without the newline), so Docker never splits a line (16 KiB). This schema is the structure; CONVENTIONS.md "Logging (log-record.v1)" has the rules a schema can't hold (masking, the catalogue, levels, sizes, dedup) and contract-check (--logs) checks both. Writers only: strict (unevaluatedProperties: false), so event-specific fields go in attrs. Readers (Fluent Bit, Loki, an analyst, an AI) ignore unknown fields. The masking classes (masking/cases.v1.json, masking/billing.v1.json) apply to every field at every depth; envelope names are chosen so that none of them classifies as phone, secret or email.

ts.description: Wall-clock time the record was made: RFC 3339, UTC, exactly 3 fractional digits, 'Z'.

version.description: The build: a semver, a git sha, or both (0.4.2+3f9c2ab).

instance.description: This process's stable name: the pod, container or replica id.

incarnation.description: Where the service has one (parity-telephony-controller's incarnation, a process start id): changes on every start of the same instance.

seq.description: Per (service, instance, incarnation): 1 for the first record of the process, +1 per record made, including those later dropped. Orders records within one millisecond; a gap is a dropped record.

event.description: A stable name from the service's catalogue (logging/events.<service>.v1.json) or logging/events.common.v1.json: dotted snake_case, noun then past-tense verb (offer.sent, leg.answered).

msg.description: Short and human, a constant per call site: values go in fields, never interpolated.

component.description: The module or class that logged: ie_core::queue, parity.gateway.agents.OfferRelay.

op.description: The RPC, handler, command or consumer being served: parity.routing.v1.RoutingService/Enqueue, POST /v1/calls, interaction.commands:redirect.

from_state.description: A state machine transition: the state left (named from_state, not state_from: the masking rules treat names ending _from or _to as phone numbers).

to_state.description: A state machine transition: the state entered.

cause.description: What triggered this record, as <kind>:<reference>: event:<event_id>, rpc:<method>, cmd:<command id>, timer:<name>, sip:<method or status>, http:<method path>, kafka:<topic>, ws:<frame type>, signal:<name>, operator:<action>, config:<name>, startup:<step>, internal:<name>. Never an exception class (that is error.kind).

duration_ms.description: How long the operation took (fractions allowed).

attempt.description: 1 for the first try of a retried operation.

code.description: The contract error code (CONVENTIONS "Error codes", a gRPC parity-error, a reply code): stale_owner, not_found, unavailable.

kind.description: The error's type: a Java exception class, a Rust error enum variant, an errno name.

message.description: The error's text, masked like any field.

stack.description: Level error or fatal only. The whole stack in one JSON string: frames separated by \n, causes as 'caused by: <kind>: <message>' lines, at most 30 frames per throwable, cut at 8192 characters with a final '...[truncated]'.

code.description: Where the record was made, when the language gives it cheaply (Rust tracing metadata, C++ __FILE__/__LINE__); Java only at warn and above.

trace_id.description: From the W3C traceparent of the work being done.

xsid.description: The cross-system call id: the interaction's id, one per customer call, the same in every service and on every leg (CONVENTIONS "The xsid"). Required on call-scoped events. UUIDv7, lowercase.

parent_xsid.description: The call that caused this one (a consult, a callback, an outbound call made from a call). Never equal to xsid.

interaction_id.description: Accepted while services move to xsid; equal to xsid when both are present.

call_id.description: parity-voice-api's CPaaS call id (= the interaction id). Never a SIP Call-ID: that is attrs.sip_call_id, masked as a phone number.

session_id.description: A session that isn't a call: an agent desktop session (gateway), a web session (frontend, admin-console), a checkout session (billing).

request_id.description: An HTTP or Kafka request's id (X-Request-Id, a request's id field).

command_id.description: A command's id: interaction.commands id, a gRPC command_id.

event_id.description: The Kafka event this record is about (published or consumed).

op_id.description: 0.16.0: the operation id, one per confirmed operator action (parity-cc-tools, admin-console's onboarding, or a system's own action such as an automatic rollback): the xsid of an operation, on every saga, event, command and record the action causes (CONVENTIONS "The op_id"). UUIDv7, lowercase.

saga_id.description: 0.16.0: the saga the record is about (parity-rs's tenant routing sagas, parity-cc-tools' service-control sagas). UUIDv7.

parent_saga_id.description: 0.16.0: the saga that started this one (a rollout's or a drain's unit move). UUIDv7.

node.description: A media node (parity-ms / freeswitch host) id.

repeat_count.description: Identical records (same event, error.code, error.kind and dedup key) held back since the last one written; this record stands for them.

repeat_since.description: When the first held-back record was made (format of ts).

attrs.description: The event's own fields (its catalogue entry names the required ones). Masked per class like everything else; at most 32 keys.

decision.description: Why a routing or optimizer decision came out as it did. Debug or trace level, or info with sampled: true (a sampled fraction, the rate in the service's catalogue entry). At most 4096 bytes serialized (contract-check). Candidates are the best few, not all: total says how many were considered.

kind.description: What was decided: agent.select, queue.select, weight.update, overflow.apply.

total.description: Candidates considered, including those not listed.

chosen.description: The chosen candidate's id; null when nothing was chosen (reason says why).

reason.description: A short code-like phrase: best_score, only_eligible, sla_breach_override, no_eligible_agent.

parts.description: The score's terms by name (skill_match, idle_s, proficiency, sla_pressure).

reason.description: Why it lost or was ineligible.
